title: Gogo Sorghum Porridge with Milk
localName: Uji wa Mtama na Maziwa — Wagogo
community: Gogo people of Dodoma — the dry season supplemented breakfast
author: Mama Salima
desc: Gogo Sorghum Milk Porridge — sorghum flour cooked into a smooth porridge and enriched with milk and honey in the Gogo tradition. The fortified breakfast of the dry Dodoma plateau — when sorghum is supplemented with cattle milk, it becomes one of Tanzania's most nutritionally complete traditional breakfasts.
longDesc: In the Gogo tradition, cattle milk is the supplement that transforms the sorghum breakfast from a simple grain porridge into a complete, high-protein meal. During the dry season when milk is available from cattle, the Gogo enrich their morning sorghum with fresh milk — combining the mineral richness of sorghum with the calcium and protein of milk.
steps: Whisk sorghum flour with ½ cup cold water until smooth.
Bring remaining water to a simmer.
Add flour paste slowly, whisking constantly.
Add milk. Stir. Heat gently — do not boil after adding milk.
chefTips: Do not boil after adding milk.
cookingScience: See TZA246 for sorghum porridge science and TZA253 for milk addition science.
sustainabilityTips: Gogo cattle herding in the dry Dodoma environment is carefully adapted to the region's carrying capacity.
culturalNote: Gogo sorghum milk porridge is the taste of Dodoma's good seasons — when the cattle are giving milk and the rains have been adequate. In a landscape of scarcity, this breakfast represents abundance.
